actions.text: Ha! Two-legs with sharp sticks! Skraag takes the farms, Skraag takes the Seal, Skraag takes YOU!
Boys! Cut them down!
Nobody passes Skraag's camp! Hee hee!
More soft ones! Smash them!
...A SMALL FIRE... IN MY WOOD... THE THORNS... SANG ME... A WARM SONG...
NOW... THE SONG IS BROKEN. I AM... AWAKE. WHO... WALKS... UNDER MY BOUGHS?
Stay back! The Oak's heart is awake, and the thorns have my legs pinned. It will go for you first!
Strike at the Briarmaw, quickly! I can hold on.
You did it. I felt the Oak let go of the whole Wood. I thought I was done for.
Take the Warden's Seal to Mayor Orrin. It will open the cave. I'll catch my breath, then follow the trail home.
Go on, hurry to the mayor. The Seal is yours. Mind the cave: older things than goblins sleep down there.
Silk glimmers between the trunks. Something large and many-legged drops down in front of you.

npcs.name: Mossbeard
npcs.title: Forest hermit
npcs.line: Hm? Oh, travellers. The Oak is older than the island's name. It sings to the thorns. Lately somebody has been singing back.

npcs.name: Garrick
npcs.title: Hunter
npcs.line: Mind yourself in there. Goblins on the trails, spiders in the hollows, and worse to the north. Rest at the ranger's camp by the pool if you need it. Follow the water.

actions.text: THE WHISPERING WOOD. Goblins on the trail; something worse in the north. Pools and a ranger's camp are to the east. TURN BACK IF YOU ARE ALONE.

Day 1. Goblin raiders are stealing from the farms. The trail is full of them. Day 2. Their chief, Skraag, keeps a thorn-totem at his camp in the north-east, and the totem is feeding brambles across the north trail. Day 3. The totem hums at night. Whatever is under the Old Oak answers it. I carry the Warden's Seal north to end this. If you read this, Ranger Willa has not come back.
The ranger's fire still holds some heat. You rest a while by the pool, and the water's sound washes the fight out of you.
A wall of black brambles, thick as your arm, humming with some wrong, borrowed life. Blades slide off it. Something is feeding it from far away.
Willa's journal said the goblin chieftain keeps a totem in his camp in the north-east. Perhaps the thorns die with it.

From up here you can see the whole Wood. The pool is south-east of the island's heart, the goblin camp lies north-east, and the oldest tree stands far to the north, behind a wall of thorns. I do not go there.
Spare arrows, salt pork, and a charm against the Oak. If you are reading this, Willa, they got further than I did. Keep the Seal off the ground; the thorns grow where it falls.
Clear, cold water wells up between the roots. It tastes of rain, and for a moment every ache leaves you.

objectives.text: Speak with Mayor Orrin in the village first
Find Ranger Willa. Follow the water, and find who feeds the thorn barrier (goblin camp in the north-east)
Cut through the withered brambles on the north trail and reach the Old Oak Grove
Speak with Ranger Willa in the grove
Take the Warden's Seal back to Mayor Orrin
The Wood is quiet. Explore for treasure, or head to the cave

actions.text: Skraag's totem cracks and goes dark. Far to the north, a groan of splintering thorns rolls through the trees. The way to the Old Oak is open.

encounters.text: Something rustles in the undergrowth... monsters attack!
